html.title: My App - Project Template
html.description: A Rust web service template with a layered skeleton, built-in authentication, and a Next.js public site. Ships with no business domain.

hero.badge: A project template built for long-term evolution
hero.subtitle: A layered modular monolith in Rust with authentication built in. No business domain inside, so every derived project starts its own from scratch.
hero.highlightAuth: Auth works out of the box

features.sectionSubtitle: The template only promises engineering capabilities; business boundaries are yours

architecture.title: Layered backend architecture
architecture.description: api / core / engines / infrastructure are separate Cargo crates that depend inwards on core, guarded by the compiler and a dependency-direction test.

authDomains.title: Secure sign-in
authDomains.description: Email and password with argon2id hashing, HttpOnly cookie sessions stored in Redis, and rate limiting on sign-in and registration.

frontends.title: Public site skeleton
frontends.description: A Next.js site with registration, sign-in and a protected area, talking to the backend only over /api/* HTTP.

observability.title: Probes and logging
observability.description: /live, /health and /ready probes, structured tracing logs, and graceful shutdown on SIGTERM.

config.title: Unified configuration
config.description: Three layers: environment variables, config.toml, and code defaults. Secrets only ever live in environment variables or .env.local.

teamwork.title: Team engineering
teamwork.description: just task runner, clippy with warnings denied, sqlx migrations, and a dependency-direction guard test, all ready to use.

steps.sectionSubtitle: Copy the template, configure the environment, start the services

copy.title: Copy the template
copy.description: Copy the repository into a new directory and rename it (see docs/migration-status.md).

configure.title: Configure the environment
configure.description: Fill in the database, Redis, and initial admin following .env.example.

run.title: Start the services
run.description: Run just sync dev to install dependencies, then just run to boot the backend and both frontends.

faq.sectionSubtitle: Things you may want to know about this template

audience.question: What kind of project is this template for?
audience.answer: Long-lived Rust web services: a clear layered skeleton and engineering facilities first, then business modules on top.

businessCode.question: Does the template ship business code?
businessCode.answer: No business domain is included. Auth, configuration, health probes, and persistence are the only skeleton; derived projects add their own business modules.

createProject.question: How do I create a new project from the template?
createProject.answer: Copy the repository into a new directory and follow the renaming steps in docs/migration-status.md. An automated just copy command has not been ported yet.

cta.title: Ready to get started?
cta.body: Create an account, enter the protected area, and build your business on a clean backend skeleton.

aboutPage.title: About this template
aboutPage.description: A Rust template for starting new projects: a layered backend skeleton, built-in authentication, and complete engineering facilities. It deliberately ships no business domain, so every derived project builds its own from a clean starting point.

simple.title: Simplicity first
simple.description: Strip the unnecessary complexity and keep only what is genuinely reusable.

security.title: Security first
security.description: From authentication to data storage, security is always the top priority.

evolution.title: Continuous evolution
evolution.description: The skeleton keeps improving while business boundaries stay with derived projects.

dashboard.title: Workspace
dashboard.gettingStartedBody: This template keeps only auth and infrastructure, with no business domain included. Add your own modules on the layered architecture: define use cases and ports under crates/core/, implement them under crates/infrastructure/ or crates/engines/, and expose HTTP routes under crates/api/.
